items.text: – Lee, tinye ya na friza. Ọ bụrụ na ị tinye ya na friza, ọ dịghị ihe ga-emerụ ya, ọbụladị ruo otu afọ. Ihe ọ bụla ọzọ fọdụrụ, tinyekwa ya na friza.
items.q: A mother mentions the freezer. Is 'friza' the everyday word for a home freezer, correctly spelled and inflected here?
before: – Ee, e rila m ha, Nini-jan. Echegbula onwe gị. Naanị obere lavashak nke Mahboub mere ka fọdụrụ.

items.text: Agwara m Mahboub na ndị ọzọ – ụmụaka, nke a bụ Covid. Na njedebe, Mahboub kpọrọ oku, ha jiri ụgbọ ala ndị ọrịa bịa buru Naney – ha sịrị ee, ọ bụ Covid.
items.q: A mother talks about an ambulance. Is 'ụgbọ ala ndị ọrịa' how people usually say it, correctly spelled here?
before: – Ma ha akpaghị ọma, nke ahụ bụ ihe merenụ. Ugbu a, Nna nna anaghị anụ ihe ọbụla ma ọ maghịkwa ihe na-eme, ma agwara m Naney ugboro ọtụtụ: Haaj Khanom, ị na-anọdụ ala n'ámá, ị ga-enweta Covid, ka Chineke ghara ikwe. Nke ahụ mere ka ọ na-anọdụ ala n'ámá karịa. Ma Amir, obi Naney na-akpọ ụda dị njọ nke ukwuu.
